title: Learning Balanced Tree Indexes for Large-Scale Vector Retrieval

problem.claim: Vector retrieval seeks k-nearest neighbors over data points and is widely used in information retrieval and recommender systems.

gap.claim: Existing state-of-the-art HNSW methods have large memory footprints, while space-partitioning learned indexes require substantial labeled data for supervised learning and may be affected in generalization by model complexity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vector retrieval is used to find k-nearest neighbors and supports information retrieval and recommender systems.
HNSW indexes typically consume substantial memory, limiting the scale of directly handled data unless external storage is used in a hybrid index.
Space-partitioning learned indexes use relatively little memory and have recently advanced substantially.
These learned indexes depend on large amounts of labeled data for supervised learning, and model complexity influences generalization.

source_observation.claim: Memory footprint is a key constraint for scaling vector-retrieval indexes.

interpretation.claim: Index design involves a tradeoff between memory usage and the ability to handle large datasets.

application.claim: When designing large-scale vector retrieval systems, evaluate index memory requirements alongside retrieval capability.

exception.claim: External storage through a hybrid index can be used when an in-memory index cannot handle the data scale.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed method or its concrete contributions.
